root_cause.text: On UP (uniprocessor) kernels, spin_trylock() is a no-op that unconditionally succeeds regardless of lock state, allowing alloc_frozen_pages_nolock() called from NMI context to re-enter rmqueue() and acquire an already-held zone lock, corrupting the freelists.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds an early return check `if (!IS_ENABLED(CONFIG_SMP) && in_nmi()) return NULL;` to prevent NMI-context calls on UP kernels from proceeding to rmqueue(). The CVE description explicitly states that "On UP kernels (!CONFIG_SMP), spin_trylock() is a no-op that unconditionally succeeds even when the lock is already held" and that this causes the function to "re-enter rmqueue() and acquire the zone lock that the interrupted context is already holding, corrupting the freelists." The stack trace shows the lock acquisition attempt in rmqueue() being called from alloc_frozen_pages_nolock_noprof() within NMI context.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add NMI guard for uniprocessor systems to prevent spin_trylock() from succeeding when lock is held on UP kernels.
intent_record.what: Added a new conditional guard that returns NULL when CONFIG_SMP is disabled and the code is executing in NMI context, with an explanatory comment about spin_trylock() behavior on uniprocessor systems.
intent_record.how: This prevents alloc_frozen_pages_nolock_noprof() from proceeding in a scenario where spin_trylock() would incorrectly succeed despite being locked on UP (uniprocessor) systems during NMI handling. On UP systems without SMP, spin_trylock() always succeeds even when the lock is held, which could cause incorrect behavior. The guard ensures the function fails safely in this problematic condition.

relevance_review.reason: The group directly addresses the root cause by adding an NMI guard for uniprocessor systems. The vulnerability occurs because spin_trylock() is a no-op on UP kernels, allowing NMI context re-entry into rmqueue() with an already-held lock. This fix prevents that re-entry scenario by guarding against NMI calls on UP systems, which is the core issue described in the root cause.

candidates.rationale: This guard condition is insufficient because it only protects against NMI/hardirq re-entrance on PREEMPT_RT kernels. On UP (uniprocessor) non-PREEMPT_RT kernels, spin_trylock() is a no-op that always succeeds, so the missing guard allows alloc_frozen_pages_nolock() called from NMI context to re-enter rmqueue() and corrupt freelists by acquiring an already-held zone lock.

vuln_statements.explanation: This conditional guard is insufficient because it only protects against NMI/hardirq re-entrance when CONFIG_PREEMPT_RT is enabled. On UP (uniprocessor) non-PREEMPT_RT kernels, spin_trylock() is a no-op that unconditionally succeeds regardless of lock state. When alloc_frozen_pages_nolock() is called from NMI context on such systems, this guard fails to prevent re-entrance into rmqueue(), allowing the function to acquire an already-held zone lock and corrupt the freelists. The guard should also check for NMI/hardirq context on UP kernels without PREEMPT_RT enabled.

bic_trace_step.reason: The commit introduces try_alloc_pages_noprof() which implements proper safeguards against the vulnerability described. The root cause is that on UP kernels, spin_trylock() is a no-op that unconditionally succeeds, allowing re-entrancy from NMI context. This commit addresses this through multiple mechanisms: (1) Lines 7126-7130 check 'if (IS_ENABLED(CONFIG_PREEMPT_RT) && (in_nmi() || in_hardirq())) return NULL;' which bails out early in NMI/hard IRQ contexts where spin_trylock would be unsafe. (2) Lines 2310-2313 and 2914-2917 modify rmqueue_bulk() and rmqueue_buddy() to use spin_trylock_irqsave() instead of unconditional spin_lock_irqsave(), and if trylock fails with ALLOC_TRYLOCK flag set, they return early instead of blocking. (3) Line 7127 sets 'alloc_flags = ALLOC_TRYLOCK;' which signals the allocator to use trylock semantics. (4) Lines 4527-4529 skip the should_fail_alloc_page() call when ALLOC_TRYLOCK is set, avoiding potential lock-taking in that path. These changes prevent the re-entrancy scenario where NMI context could acquire an already-held zone lock by ensuring early bailout in unsafe contexts and using non-blocking trylock operations.
